messages:
elaine (AE): Quick heads-up — Pacifica (healthcare) wants to run a 6‑week POC for a clinical triage/QA assistant. They flagged HIPAA, EU data residency, and want SOC2 + pen‑test artifacts before infra access. Also asking about hosted vs dedicated pricing and a hard cap for POC spend. Can we scope?

matt (sales_eng): Adding SE/security. Quick clarifying Qs: will they send PHI in live prompts or only synthetic for evals? If PHI yes -> Private/VPC or Dedicated with strict controls. Also need rough estimate for 5k requests/day baseline.

jordan (pacifica): They'll have some PHI (patient initials, visit dates, limited identifiers) in real integration, but for initial eval they can give synthetic or redacted samples. EU residency required for production. Execs want a firm POC spend cap.

anya (solutions): Recommendation: run POC on Dedicated with VPC peering for speed + data isolation, or Private if they insist on customer-managed control. For a fast 6‑week proof: reserve 2x A100-equivalent GPUs, routing policy to EU region. Success criteria we should propose: p95 latency < 400ms, accuracy >= 85% on curated eval set, zero PII leakage observed in outputs. I'll draft prompts and an eval harness.

julian (security): We can provide SOC2 Type II report and a redacted pen‑test summary. For HIPAA/BAA we need a signed BAA + DPA covering EU flows. Security controls they specifically asked about: KMS/HSM integration, no persistent logging of full prompts, ability to disable request logging, ephemeral KV cache, and customer-managed keys preferred. If external pen‑test requested by Pacifica, we need to scope attack surface first.

tess (legal): Legal review for DPA/BAA typically ~2–3 weeks. We'll need a data flow diagram and list of subprocessors to confirm EU residency compliance. We can start preparing template BAA text.

ran (cs): I can own the eval plan. Ask Pacifica for 200 sample convos (synthetic okay) and a list of typical prompt patterns + expected labels. We'll run automated batch evals + adversarial PII leakage scans and return a short report.

jordan (pacifica): Will collect samples. Also request: can Redwood issue a temporary SOC2 attestation and a pen‑test scope ASAP? Their security team wants to review before integration.

matt (sales_eng): On pricing/quotas: we can put a hard quota and billing alert in place. Ballpark estimate for a 6‑week Dedicated POC (2 GPUs, reserved burst, support + monitoring): ~$12k–$18k. Hosted with strict settings (no logs, EU region) would be cheaper but requires additional contractual controls — pricing closer to $6k–$9k. Can offer credits depending on path. I'll confirm exact quote with finance. :money_with_wings:

anya (solutions): Draft of eval rubric (short):
```
- Relevance: micro-F1 >= 0.85 on labeled set
- Hallucination: < 5% of responses flagged by human review
- Latency: p95 < 400ms in EU region under 5rps baseline
- PII leakage: 0 high-severity leakage incidents on adversarial tests
```
I'll push a small sample harness so they can run locally against synthetic data.

julian (security): For pen‑test scoping — we need answers to: admin endpoints, SSO provider, which ports are open, whether SFTP/agents will run in their network, and if any connectors will store keys locally. We'll provide a pen‑test scoping template they can fill. Once scoped, we can either: 1) run internal red team and share a redacted report, or 2) allow an approved external tester after contractual sign-off.

elaine (AE): Action items: @jordan — send 200 sample convos (synthetic ok) + a data flow diagram for EU residency; @matt — preliminary quote and quota proposal; @julian + @tess — prep SOC2/BAA artifacts and pen‑test scoping template; @ran — draft eval rubric and harness. Sync Thursday 10:00am PT to align. :thumbsup:

redwood-bot: Reminder: create POC workspace + billing alert -- template created.
